occupations.title: Chief Executives
occupations.description: Determine and formulate policies and provide overall direction of companies or private and public sector organizations within guidelines set up by a board of directors or similar governing body. Plan, direct, or coordinate operational activities at the highest level of management with the help of subordinate executives and staff managers.

occupations.title: Chief Sustainability Officers
occupations.description: Communicate and coordinate with management, shareholders, customers, and employees to address sustainability issues. Enact or oversee a corporate sustainability strategy.

titles.text: CSR and Sustainability VP (Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Vice President)
ESG Manager (Environmental, Social, and Corporate Governance Manager)
Sustainability Initiatives Vice President (Sustainability Initiatives VP)

occupations.title: General and Operations Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate the operations of public or private sector organizations, overseeing multiple departments or locations. Duties and responsibilities include formulating policies, managing daily operations, and planning the use of materials and human resources, but are too diverse and general in nature to be classified in any one functional area of management or administration, such as personnel, purchasing, or administrative services. Usually manage through subordinate supervisors. Excludes First-Line Supervisors.

titles.text: Department Store General Manager (Dept Store GM)

occupations.title: Legislators
occupations.description: Develop, introduce, or enact laws and statutes at the local, tribal, state, or federal level. Includes only workers in elected positions.

occupations.title: Advertising and Promotions Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate advertising policies and programs or produce collateral materials, such as posters, contests, coupons, or giveaways, to create extra interest in the purchase of a product or service for a department, an entire organization, or on an account basis.

occupations.title: Marketing Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate marketing policies and programs, such as determining the demand for products and services offered by a firm and its competitors, and identify potential customers. Develop pricing strategies with the goal of maximizing the firm's profits or share of the market while ensuring the firm's customers are satisfied. Oversee product development or monitor trends that indicate the need for new products and services.

occupations.title: Sales Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate the actual distribution or movement of a product or service to the customer. Coordinate sales distribution by establishing sales territories, quotas, and goals and establish training programs for sales representatives. Analyze sales statistics gathered by staff to determine sales potential and inventory requirements and monitor the preferences of customers.

titles.text: Professional Equipment Sales and Service Manager
Sales and Marketing VP (Sales and Marketing Vice President)

occupations.title: Public Relations Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate activities designed to create or maintain a favorable public image or raise issue awareness for their organization or client.

occupations.title: Fundraising Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate activities to solicit and maintain funds for special projects or nonprofit organizations.

titles.text: Institutional Advancement VP (Institutional Advancement Vice President)

occupations.title: Administrative Services Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate one or more administrative services of an organization, such as records and information management, mail distribution, and other office support services.

occupations.title: Facilities Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate operations and functionalities of facilities and buildings. May include surrounding grounds or multiple facilities of an organization's campus.

occupations.title: Security Managers
occupations.description: Direct an organization's security functions, including physical security and safety of employees and facilities.

titles.text: IS Security Manager (Information Systems Security Manager)

occupations.title: Computer and Information Systems Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate activities in such fields as electronic data processing, information systems, systems analysis, and computer programming.

titles.text: Information Technology Account Manager (IT Account Manager)
IT Infrastructure Director (Information Technology Infrastructure Director)
IT Portfolio Manager (Information Technology Portfolio Manager)
Programming and Software Development Project Manager

occupations.title: Financial Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate accounting, investing, banking, insurance, securities, and other financial activities of a branch, office, or department of an establishment.

occupations.title: Treasurers and Controllers
occupations.description: Direct financial activities, such as planning, procurement, and investments for all or part of an organization.

occupations.title: Investment Fund Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate investment strategy or operations for a large pool of liquid assets supplied by institutional investors or individual investors.

titles.text: Financial Planning and Analysis Finance Manager
Fixed Income Vice President (Fixed Income VP)
Investment Analysis Vice President (Investment Analysis VP)

occupations.title: Industrial Production Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate the work activities and resources necessary for manufacturing products in accordance with cost, quality, and quantity specifications.

occupations.title: Quality Control Systems Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate quality assurance programs. Formulate quality control policies and control quality of laboratory and production efforts.

titles.text: Quality Control Microbiology Supervisor (QC Microbiology Supervisor)
Quality Control Systems Manager (QC Systems Manager)

occupations.title: Geothermal Production Managers
occupations.description: Manage operations at geothermal power generation facilities. Maintain and monitor geothermal plant equipment for efficient and safe plant operations.

occupations.title: Biofuels Production Managers
occupations.description: Manage biofuels production and plant operations. Collect and process information on plant production and performance, diagnose problems, and design corrective procedures.

occupations.title: Biomass Power Plant Managers
occupations.description: Manage operations at biomass power generation facilities. Direct work activities at plant, including supervision of operations and maintenance staff.

occupations.title: Hydroelectric Production Managers
occupations.description: Manage operations at hydroelectric power generation facilities. Maintain and monitor hydroelectric plant equipment for efficient and safe plant operations.

titles.text: Hydroelectric Plant Site Manager (Hydro Plant Site Manager)

occupations.title: Purchasing Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate the activities of buyers, purchasing officers, and related workers involved in purchasing materials, products, and services. Includes wholesale or retail trade merchandising managers and procurement managers.

occupations.title: Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate transportation, storage, or distribution activities in accordance with organizational policies and applicable government laws or regulations. Includes logistics managers.

titles.text: Railroad Car Inspection and Repair Regional Superintendent

occupations.title: Supply Chain Managers
occupations.description: Direct or coordinate production, purchasing, warehousing, distribution, or financial forecasting services or activities to limit costs and improve accuracy, customer service, or safety. Examine existing procedures or opportunities for streamlining activities to meet product distribution needs. Direct the movement, storage, or processing of inventory.

occupations.title: Compensation and Benefits Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate compensation and benefits activities of an organization.

titles.text: Wage and Salary Administrator (Wage and Salary Admin)

occupations.title: Human Resources Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate human resources activities and staff of an organization.

titles.text: HR Admin Director (Human Resources Administration Director)
HR Department Supervisor (Human Resources Department Supervisor)
HR Ops Manager (Human Resources Operations Manager)

occupations.title: Training and Development Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate the training and development activities and staff of an organization.

titles.text: L and D Director (Learning and Development Director)
L and D Program Manager (Learning and Development Program Manager)
Training and Development Coordinator (T and D Coordinator)
Training and Development Director (T and D Director)
Training and Development Manager (T and D Manager)

occupations.title: Farmers, Ranchers, and Other Agricultural Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate the management or operation of farms, ranches, greenhouses, aquacultural operations, nurseries, timber tracts, or other agricultural establishments. May hire, train, and supervise farm workers or contract for services to carry out the day-to-day activities of the managed operation. May engage in or supervise planting, cultivating, harvesting, and financial and marketing activities.

titles.text: Crop, Grain, or Livestock Farm Manager
Fruit or Nut Crops Farm Manager

occupations.title: Construction Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate, usually through subordinate supervisory personnel, activities concerned with the construction and maintenance of structures, facilities, and systems. Participate in the conceptual development of a construction project and oversee its organization, scheduling, budgeting, and implementation. Includes managers in specialized construction fields, such as carpentry or plumbing.

occupations.title: Education and Childcare Administrators, Preschool and Daycare
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate academic or nonacademic activities of preschools or childcare centers and programs, including before- and after-school care.

titles.text: Before and After School Program Director
Before and After School Site Director
Child Care Center Administrator (Child Care Center Admin)

occupations.title: Education Administrators, Kindergarten through Secondary
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate the academic, administrative, or auxiliary activities of kindergarten, elementary, or secondary schools.

titles.text: Junior HS Principal (Junior High School Principal)
K-12 Principal (Kindergarten Through Twelfth Grade Principal)
K-12 School Principal (Kindergarten Through Twelfth Grade School Principal)
K-8 School Principal (Kindergarten Through Eighth Grade School Principal)

occupations.title: Education Administrators, Postsecondary
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate student instruction, administration, and services, as well as other research and educational activities, at postsecondary institutions, including universities, colleges, and junior and community colleges.

titles.text: Academic Affairs Vice President (Academic Affairs VP)
Enrollment Management Vice President (Enrollment Management VP)
Enrollment Services Vice President (Enrollment Services VP)
Student Affairs Vice President (Student Affairs VP)

occupations.title: Education Administrators, All Other
occupations.description: All education administrators not listed separately.

occupations.title: Architectural and Engineering Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate activities in such fields as architecture and engineering or research and development in these fields.

occupations.title: Biofuels/Biodiesel Technology and Product Development Managers
occupations.description: Define, plan, or execute biofuels/biodiesel research programs that evaluate alternative feedstock and process technologies with near-term commercial potential.

titles.text: Business Development and New Technology Manager

occupations.title: Food Service Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate activities of an organization or department that serves food and beverages.

titles.text: F and B Director (Food and Beverage Director)
F and B Manager (Food and Beverage Manager)
Food Service GM (Food Service General Manager)

occupations.title: Gambling Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate gambling operations in a casino. May formulate house rules.

occupations.title: Entertainment and Recreation Managers, Except Gambling
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate entertainment and recreational activities and operations of a recreational facility, including cruise ships and parks.

titles.text: Entertainment and Recreation GM (Entertainment and Recreation General Manager)
Entertainment and Recreation Operations Manager (Entertainment and Recreation Ops Manager)
Entertainment and Recreation PM (Entertainment and Recreation Project Manager)

occupations.title: Lodging Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate activities of an organization or department that provides lodging and other accommodations.

titles.text: RV Resort Manager (Recreational Vehicle Resort Manager)

occupations.title: Medical and Health Services Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate medical and health services in hospitals, clinics, managed care organizations, public health agencies, or similar organizations.

occupations.title: Natural Sciences Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate activities in such fields as life sciences, physical sciences, mathematics, statistics, and research and development in these fields.

titles.text: Laboratory Services Administrative Director (Lab Services Administrative Director)
Research and Development Director (R and D Director)
Research and Development Manager (R & D Manager)

occupations.title: Clinical Research Coordinators
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate clinical research projects. Direct the activities of workers engaged in clinical research projects to ensure compliance with protocols and overall clinical objectives. May evaluate and analyze clinical data.

occupations.title: Water Resource Specialists
occupations.description: Design or implement programs and strategies related to water resource issues such as supply, quality, and regulatory compliance issues.

occupations.title: Postmasters and Mail Superintendents
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate operational, administrative, management, and support services of a U.S. post office; or coordinate activities of workers engaged in postal and related work in assigned post office.

occupations.title: Property, Real Estate, and Community Association Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate the selling, buying, leasing, or governance activities of commercial, industrial, or residential real estate properties. Includes managers of homeowner and condominium associations, rented or leased housing units, buildings, or land (including rights-of-way).

occupations.title: Social and Community Service Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate the activities of a social service program or community outreach organization. Oversee the program or organization's budget and policies regarding participant involvement, program requirements, and benefits. Work may involve directing social workers, counselors, or probation officers.

occupations.title: Emergency Management Directors
occupations.description: Plan and direct disaster response or crisis management activities, provide disaster preparedness training, and prepare emergency plans and procedures for natural (e.g., hurricanes, floods, earthquakes), wartime, or technological (e.g., nuclear power plant emergencies or hazardous materials spills) disasters or hostage situations.

occupations.title: Funeral Home Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate the services or resources of funeral homes. Includes activities such as determining prices for services or merchandise and managing the facilities of funeral homes.

titles.text: Funeral Home GM (Funeral Home General Manager)

occupations.title: Personal Service Managers, All Other
occupations.description: All personal service managers not listed separately.

occupations.title: Fitness and Wellness Coordinators
occupations.description: Manage or coordinate fitness and wellness programs and services. Manage and train staff of wellness specialists, health educators, or fitness instructors.

titles.text: Employee Assistance Program Wellness Coordinator (EAP Wellness Coordinator)

occupations.title: Spa Managers
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate activities of a spa facility. Coordinate programs, schedule and direct staff, and oversee financial activities.

occupations.title: Managers, All Other
occupations.description: All managers not listed separately.

titles.text: Chamber of Commerce Executive Vice President
Leased Machinery and Equipment Service Supervisor
State Board of Nursing Educational Consultant

occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate production activities of an organization to ensure compliance with regulations and standard operating procedures.

Governance Compliance and Risk Manager (GCR Manager)
Health Information Management Privacy and Security Officer
Health, Safety, and Environmental Manager (HSE Manager)

occupations.title: Loss Prevention Managers
occupations.description: Plan and direct policies, procedures, or systems to prevent the loss of assets. Determine risk exposure or potential liability, and develop risk control measures.

occupations.title: Wind Energy Operations Managers
occupations.description: Manage wind field operations, including personnel, maintenance activities, financial activities, and planning.

titles.text: Energy Quality Control Manager (Energy QC Manager)

occupations.title: Wind Energy Development Managers
occupations.description: Lead or manage the development and evaluation of potential wind energy business opportunities, including environmental studies, permitting, and proposals. May also manage construction of projects.

titles.text: Renewable Project Management and Construction Director

occupations.title: Brownfield Redevelopment Specialists and Site Managers
occupations.description: Plan and direct cleanup and redevelopment of contaminated properties for reuse. Does not include properties sufficiently contaminated to qualify as Superfund sites.

occupations.title: Agents and Business Managers of Artists, Performers, and Athletes
occupations.description: Represent and promote artists, performers, and athletes in dealings with current or prospective employers. May handle contract negotiation and other business matters for clients.

occupations.title: Buyers and Purchasing Agents, Farm Products
occupations.description: Purchase farm products either for further processing or resale. Includes tree farm contractors, grain brokers and market operators, grain buyers, and tobacco buyers. May negotiate contracts.

titles.text: Livestock, Grain, Cotton and Other Farm Products Purchasing Agent

occupations.title: Wholesale and Retail Buyers, Except Farm Products
occupations.description: Buy merchandise or commodities, other than farm products, for resale to consumers at the wholesale or retail level, including both durable and nondurable goods. Analyze past buying trends, sales records, price, and quality of merchandise to determine value and yield. Select, order, and authorize payment for merchandise according to contractual agreements. May conduct meetings with sales personnel and introduce new products. May negotiate contracts. Includes assistant wholesale and retail buyers of nonfarm products.

occupations.title: Purchasing Agents, Except Wholesale, Retail, and Farm Products
occupations.description: Purchase machinery, equipment, tools, parts, supplies, or services necessary for the operation of an establishment. Purchase raw or semifinished materials for manufacturing. May negotiate contracts.

titles.text: Equipment, Supplies, and Tools Purchasing Agent
Procurement and Contracting Administrator (Procurement and Contracting Admin)
Tools, Supplies, and Equipment Purchasing Agent

occupations.title: Claims Adjusters, Examiners, and Investigators
occupations.description: Review settled claims to determine that payments and settlements are made in accordance with company practices and procedures. Confer with legal counsel on claims requiring litigation. May also settle insurance claims.

titles.text: Auto Damage Claims Adjuster (Automotive Damage Claims Adjuster)
Property and Casualty Insurance Claims Examiner

occupations.title: Insurance Appraisers, Auto Damage
occupations.description: Appraise automobile or other vehicle damage to determine repair costs for insurance claim settlement. Prepare insurance forms to indicate repair cost or cost estimates and recommendations. May seek agreement with automotive repair shop on repair costs.

titles.text: Automobile Damage Field Appraiser (Auto Damage Field Appraiser)
Automotive Body Shop Estimator (Auto Body Shop Estimator)
Field Automobile Damage Appraiser (Field Auto Damage Appraiser)

occupations.title: Compliance Officers
occupations.description: Examine, evaluate, and investigate eligibility for or conformity with laws and regulations governing contract compliance of licenses and permits, and perform other compliance and enforcement inspection and analysis activities not classified elsewhere.

titles.text: Department of Motor Vehicles Clerk (DMV Clerk)
IT Compliance Analyst (Information Technology Compliance Analyst)

occupations.title: Environmental Compliance Inspectors
occupations.description: Inspect and investigate sources of pollution to protect the public and environment and ensure conformance with Federal, State, and local regulations and ordinances.

titles.text: Certified Erosion, Sediment, and Storm Water Inspector (CESSWI)
Environmental Health and Safety Advisor (EH & S)
Resource Conservation and Recovery Act Enforcement Officer (RCRA Enforcement Officer)

occupations.title: Equal Opportunity Representatives and Officers
occupations.description: Monitor and evaluate compliance with equal opportunity laws, guidelines, and policies to ensure that employment practices and contracting arrangements give equal opportunity without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.

occupations.title: Government Property Inspectors and Investigators
occupations.description: Investigate or inspect government property to ensure compliance with contract agreements and government regulations.

occupations.title: Coroners
occupations.description: Direct activities such as autopsies, pathological and toxicological analyses, and inquests relating to the investigation of deaths occurring within a legal jurisdiction to determine cause of death or to fix responsibility for accidental, violent, or unexplained deaths.

occupations.title: Regulatory Affairs Specialists
occupations.description: Coordinate and document internal regulatory processes, such as internal audits, inspections, license renewals, or registrations. May compile and prepare materials for submission to regulatory agencies.

QA Documentation Specialist (Quality Assurance Documentation Specialist)
Research QA Analyst (Research Quality Assurance Analyst)
Research QA Specialist (Research Quality Assurance Specialist)

occupations.title: Customs Brokers
occupations.description: Prepare customs documentation and ensure that shipments meet all applicable laws to facilitate the import and export of goods. Determine and track duties and taxes payable and process payments on behalf of client. Sign documents under a power of attorney. Represent clients in meetings with customs officials and apply for duty refunds and tariff reclassifications. Coordinate transportation and storage of imported goods.

titles.text: CBP Agent (Customs and Border Patrol Agent)

occupations.title: Cost Estimators
occupations.description: Prepare cost estimates for product manufacturing, construction projects, or services to aid management in bidding on or determining price of product or service. May specialize according to particular service performed or type of product manufactured.

occupations.title: Human Resources Specialists
occupations.description: Recruit, screen, interview, or place individuals within an organization. May perform other activities in multiple human resources areas.

titles.text: HR Business Partner (Human Resources Business Partner)
HRIS Analyst (Human Resources Information System Analyst)

occupations.title: Farm Labor Contractors
occupations.description: Recruit and hire seasonal or temporary agricultural laborers. May transport, house, and provide meals for workers.

occupations.title: Labor Relations Specialists
occupations.description: Resolve disputes between workers and managers, negotiate collective bargaining agreements, or coordinate grievance procedures to handle employee complaints.

occupations.title: Logisticians
occupations.description: Analyze and coordinate the ongoing logistical functions of a firm or organization. Responsible for the entire life cycle of a product, including acquisition, distribution, internal allocation, delivery, and final disposal of resources.

occupations.title: Logistics Engineers
occupations.description: Design or analyze operational solutions for projects such as transportation optimization, network modeling, process and methods analysis, cost containment, capacity enhancement, routing and shipment optimization, or information management.

occupations.title: Logistics Analysts
occupations.description: Analyze product delivery or supply chain processes to identify or recommend changes. May manage route activity including invoicing, electronic bills, and shipment tracing.

occupations.title: Project Management Specialists
occupations.description: Analyze and coordinate the schedule, timeline, procurement, staffing, and budget of a product or service on a per project basis. Lead and guide the work of technical staff. May serve as a point of contact for the client or customer.

titles.text: HR Project Manager (Human Resources Project Manager)

occupations.title: Management Analysts
occupations.description: Conduct organizational studies and evaluations, design systems and procedures, conduct work simplification and measurement studies, and prepare operations and procedures manuals to assist management in operating more efficiently and effectively. Includes program analysts and management consultants.

titles.text: Health Information Management Business Analyst (HIM Business Analyst)
Health Information Management Data Analyst (HIM Data Analyst)

occupations.title: Meeting, Convention, and Event Planners

occupations.title: Fundraisers
occupations.description: Organize activities to raise funds or otherwise solicit and gather monetary donations or other gifts for an organization. May design and produce promotional materials. May also raise awareness of the organization's work, goals, and financial needs.

occupations.title: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
occupations.description: Conduct programs of compensation and benefits and job analysis for employer. May specialize in specific areas, such as position classification and pension programs.

titles.text: HR Benefits Specialist (Human Resources Benefits Specialist)
Payroll and Benefits Administrator (Payroll and Benefits Admin)
Salary and Wage Administrator (Salary and Wage Admin)

occupations.description: Design or conduct work-related training and development programs to improve individual skills or organizational performance. May analyze organizational training needs or evaluate training effectiveness.

IT Technical Trainer (Information Technology Technical Trainer)
Learning and Development Specialist (L and D Specialist)
Research and Development Specialist (R and D Specialist)

occupations.title: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
occupations.description: Research conditions in local, regional, national, or online markets. Gather information to determine potential sales of a product or service, or plan a marketing or advertising campaign. May gather information on competitors, prices, sales, and methods of marketing and distribution. May employ search marketing tactics, analyze web metrics, and develop recommendations to increase search engine ranking and visibility to target markets.

occupations.title: Search Marketing Strategists
occupations.description: Employ search marketing tactics to increase visibility and engagement with content, products, or services in Internet-enabled devices or interfaces. Examine search query behaviors on general or specialty search engines or other Internet-based content. Analyze research, data, or technology to understand user intent and measure outcomes for ongoing optimization.

titles.text: Internet E-Commerce Specialist (Internet Electronic Commerce Specialist)

occupations.title: Business Operations Specialists, All Other
occupations.description: All business operations specialists not listed separately.

titles.text: Business Opportunity and Property Investment Broker

occupations.description: Develop, maintain, or implement business continuity and disaster recovery strategies and solutions, including risk assessments, business impact analyses, strategy selection, and documentation of business continuity and disaster recovery procedures. Plan, conduct, and debrief regular mock-disaster exercises to test the adequacy of existing plans and strategies, updating procedures and plans regularly. Act as a coordinator for continuity efforts after a disruption event.

titles.text: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Consultant
Business Continuity And Disaster Recovery Specialist
Change Management Project Manager (Change Management PM)

occupations.title: Sustainability Specialists
occupations.description: Address organizational sustainability issues, such as waste stream management, green building practices, and green procurement plans.

titles.text: E-Commerce Digital Marketing Manager (Electronic Commerce Digital Marketing Manager)

occupations.description: Examine, analyze, and interpret accounting records to prepare financial statements, give advice, or audit and evaluate statements prepared by others. Install or advise on systems of recording costs or other financial and budgetary data.

occupations.title: Appraisers of Personal and Business Property
occupations.description: Appraise and estimate the fair value of tangible personal or business property, such as jewelry, art, antiques, collectibles, and equipment. May also appraise land.

occupations.title: Appraisers and Assessors of Real Estate
occupations.description: Appraise real estate, exclusively, and estimate its fair value. May assess taxes in accordance with prescribed schedules.

occupations.title: Budget Analysts
occupations.description: Examine budget estimates for completeness, accuracy, and conformance with procedures and regulations. Analyze budgeting and accounting reports.

titles.text: Program Cost Schedule and Control Analyst

occupations.title: Credit Analysts
occupations.description: Analyze credit data and financial statements of individuals or firms to determine the degree of risk involved in extending credit or lending money. Prepare reports with credit information for use in decisionmaking.

occupations.title: Financial and Investment Analysts
occupations.description: Conduct quantitative analyses of information involving investment programs or financial data of public or private institutions, including valuation of businesses.

titles.text: M and A Banker (Mergers and Acquisitions Banker)
Mergers and Acquisitions Associate (M and A Associate)
Mergers and Acquisitions Consultant (M and A Consultant)

occupations.description: Advise clients on financial plans using knowledge of tax and investment strategies, securities, insurance, pension plans, and real estate. Duties include assessing clients' assets, liabilities, cash flow, insurance coverage, tax status, and financial objectives. May also buy and sell financial assets for clients.

occupations.title: Insurance Underwriters
occupations.description: Review individual applications for insurance to evaluate degree of risk involved and determine acceptance of applications.

occupations.title: Financial Risk Specialists
occupations.description: Analyze and measure exposure to credit and market risk threatening the assets, earning capacity, or economic state of an organization. May make recommendations to limit risk.

occupations.title: Financial Examiners
occupations.description: Enforce or ensure compliance with laws and regulations governing financial and securities institutions and financial and real estate transactions. May examine, verify, or authenticate records.

titles.text: Bank Secrecy Act Anti-Money Laundering Officer (BSA/AML Officer)
Home Mortgage Disclosure Act Specialist (HMDA Specialist)

occupations.title: Credit Counselors
occupations.description: Advise and educate individuals or organizations on acquiring and managing debt. May provide guidance in determining the best type of loan and explain loan requirements or restrictions. May help develop debt management plans or student financial aid packages. May advise on credit issues, or provide budget, mortgage, bankruptcy, or student financial aid counseling.

titles.text: Certified Consumer Credit and Housing Counselor

occupations.title: Loan Officers
occupations.description: Evaluate, authorize, or recommend approval of commercial, real estate, or credit loans. Advise borrowers on financial status and payment methods. Includes mortgage loan officers and agents, collection analysts, loan servicing officers, loan underwriters, and payday loan officers.

occupations.title: Tax Examiners and Collectors, and Revenue Agents
occupations.description: Determine tax liability or collect taxes from individuals or business firms according to prescribed laws and regulations.

occupations.title: Tax Preparers
occupations.description: Prepare tax returns for individuals or small businesses.

titles.text: State and Local Tax Associate (SALT Associate)

occupations.title: Financial Specialists, All Other
occupations.description: All financial specialists not listed separately.

occupations.title: Financial Quantitative Analysts
occupations.description: Develop quantitative techniques to inform securities investing, equities investing, pricing, or valuation of financial instruments. Develop mathematical or statistical models for risk management, asset optimization, pricing, or relative value analysis.

occupations.title: Fraud Examiners, Investigators and Analysts
occupations.description: Obtain evidence, take statements, produce reports, and testify to findings regarding resolution of fraud allegations. May coordinate fraud detection and prevention activities.

titles.text: AML Operations Analyst (Anti-Money Laundering Operations Analyst)
SIU Clinical Investigator (Special Investigations Unit Clinical Investigator)
SIU Field Investigator (Special Investigations Unit Field Investigator)

May analyze or recommend commercially available software.

occupations.title: Biochemists and Biophysicists

May determine the effects of foods, drugs, serums, hormones, and other substances on tissues and vital processes of living organisms.

titles.text: Quality Control Microbiology Analyst (QC Microbiology Analyst)

occupations.title: Zoologists and Wildlife Biologists

occupations.title: Biological Scientists, All Other

occupations.title: Bioinformatics Scientists

occupations.title: Molecular and Cellular Biologists

occupations.title: Geneticists

occupations.title: Biologists
occupations.description: Research or study basic principles of plant and animal life, such as origin, relationship, development, anatomy, and functions.

occupations.title: Conservation Scientists

occupations.title: Foresters

May inventory the type, amount, and location of standing timber, appraise the timber's worth, negotiate the purchase, and draw up contracts for procurement. May determine how to conserve wildlife habitats, creek beds, water quality, and soil stability, and how best to comply with environmental regulations. May devise plans for planting and growing new trees, monitor trees for healthy growth, and determine optimal harvesting schedules.

occupations.title: Epidemiologists
occupations.description: Investigate and describe the determinants and distribution of disease, disability, or health outcomes. May develop the means for prevention and control.

occupations.title: Physicists

May study the Earth's internal composition, atmospheres, and oceans, and its magnetic, electrical, and gravitational forces. Includes mineralogists, paleontologists, stratigraphers, geodesists, and seismologists.

occupations.title: Hydrologists
occupations.description: Research the distribution, circulation, and physical properties of underground and surface waters; and study the form and intensity of precipitation and its rate of infiltration into the soil, movement through the earth, and return to the ocean and atmosphere.

occupations.title: Physical Scientists, All Other

occupations.description: Apply remote sensing principles and methods to analyze data and solve problems in areas such as natural resource management, urban planning, or homeland security. May develop new sensor systems, analytical techniques, or new applications for existing systems.

occupations.title: Environmental Economists
occupations.description: Conduct economic analysis related to environmental protection and use of the natural environment, such as water, air, land, and renewable energy resources. Provide individual or group counseling services to assist individuals in achieving more effective personal, social, educational, and vocational development and adjustment. May design behavior modification programs and consult with medical personnel regarding the best treatment for patients.

occupations.title: School Psychologists
occupations.description: Diagnose and implement individual or schoolwide interventions or strategies to address educational, behavioral, or developmental issues that adversely impact educational functioning in a school. occupations.title: Clinical Neuropsychologists
occupations.description: Assess and diagnose patients with neurobehavioral problems related to acquired or developmental disorders of the nervous system, such as neurodegenerative disorders, traumatic brain injury, seizure disorders, and learning disabilities. Recommend treatment after diagnosis, such as therapy, medication, or surgery. Assist with evaluation before and after neurosurgical procedures, such as deep brain stimulation.

occupations.title: Sociologists
occupations.description: Study human society and social behavior by examining the groups and social institutions that people form, as well as various social, religious, political, and business organizations. occupations.title: Urban and Regional Planners

occupations.title: Anthropologists and Archeologists
occupations.description: Study the origin, development, and behavior of human beings. May study the way of life, language, or physical characteristics of people in various parts of the world. occupations.title: Geographers
occupations.description: Study the nature and use of areas of the Earth's surface, relating and interpreting interactions of physical and cultural phenomena. Conduct research on physical aspects of a region, including land forms, climates, soils, plants, and animals, and conduct research on the spatial implications of human activities within a given area, including social characteristics, economic activities, and political organization, as well as researching interdependence between regions at scales ranging from local to global.

occupations.title: Historians

occupations.title: Political Scientists
occupations.description: Study the origin, development, and operation of political systems. May study topics, such as public opinion, political decisionmaking, and ideology. occupations.title: Set and Exhibit Designers
occupations.description: Design special exhibits and sets for film, video, television, and theater productions. May study scripts, confer with directors, and conduct research to determine appropriate architectural styles.

occupations.title: Designers, All Other
occupations.description: All designers not listed separately.

occupations.title: Actors
occupations.description: Play parts in stage, television, radio, video, or film productions, or other settings for entertainment, information, or instruction. Interpret serious or comic role by speech, gesture, and body movement to entertain or inform audience. May dance and sing.

occupations.title: Producers and Directors
occupations.description: Produce or direct stage, television, radio, video, or film productions for entertainment, information, or instruction. Responsible for creative decisions, such as interpretation of script, choice of actors or guests, set design, sound, special effects, and choreography.

occupations.title: Media Programming Directors
occupations.description: Direct and coordinate activities of personnel engaged in preparation of radio or television station program schedules and programs, such as sports or news.

titles.text: Cable TV Program Director (Cable Television Program Director)

occupations.title: Talent Directors
occupations.description: Audition and interview performers to select most appropriate talent for parts in stage, television, radio, or motion picture productions.

occupations.title: Media Technical Directors/Managers
occupations.description: Coordinate activities of technical departments, such as taping, editing, engineering, and maintenance, to produce radio or television programs.

occupations.title: Athletes and Sports Competitors
occupations.description: Compete in athletic events.

titles.text: NASCAR Driver (National Association for Stock Car Auto Racing Driver)
NASCAR Racer (National Association for Stock Car Auto Racing Racer)

occupations.title: Coaches and Scouts
occupations.description: Instruct or coach groups or individuals in the fundamentals of sports for the primary purpose of competition. Demonstrate techniques and methods of participation. May evaluate athletes' strengths and weaknesses as possible recruits or to improve the athletes' technique to prepare them for competition. Those required to hold teaching certifications should be reported in the appropriate teaching category.

occupations.title: Umpires, Referees, and Other Sports Officials
occupations.description: Officiate at competitive athletic or sporting events. Detect infractions of rules and decide penalties according to established regulations. Includes all sporting officials, referees, and competition judges.

occupations.title: Dancers
occupations.description: Perform dances. May perform on stage, for broadcasting, or for video recording.

occupations.title: Choreographers
occupations.description: Create new dance routines. Rehearse performance of routines. May direct and stage presentations.

occupations.title: Music Directors and Composers
occupations.description: Conduct, direct, plan, and lead instrumental or vocal performances by musical artists or groups, such as orchestras, bands, choirs, and glee clubs; or create original works of music.

occupations.title: Musicians and Singers
occupations.description: Play one or more musical instruments or sing. May perform on stage, for broadcasting, or for sound or video recording.

occupations.title: Disc Jockeys, Except Radio
occupations.description: Play prerecorded music for live audiences at venues or events such as clubs, parties, or wedding receptions. May use techniques such as mixing, cutting, or sampling to manipulate recordings. May also perform as emcee (master of ceremonies).

occupations.title: Entertainers and Performers, Sports and Related Workers, All Other
occupations.description: All entertainers and performers, sports and related workers not listed separately.

occupations.title: Broadcast Announcers and Radio Disc Jockeys
occupations.description: Speak or read from scripted materials, such as news reports or commercial messages, on radio, television, or other communications media. May play and queue music, announce artist or title of performance, identify station, or interview guests.

occupations.title: News Analysts, Reporters, and Journalists
occupations.description: Narrate or write news stories, reviews, or commentary for print, broadcast, or other communications media such as newspapers, magazines, radio, or television. May collect and analyze information through interview, investigation, or observation.

occupations.title: Public Relations Specialists
occupations.description: Promote or create an intended public image for individuals, groups, or organizations. May write or select material for release to various communications media. May specialize in using social media.

occupations.title: Editors
occupations.description: Plan, coordinate, revise, or edit written material. May review proposals and drafts for possible publication.

occupations.title: Technical Writers
occupations.description: Write technical materials, such as equipment manuals, appendices, or operating and maintenance instructions. May assist in layout work.

occupations.title: Writers and Authors
occupations.description: Originate and prepare written material, such as scripts, stories, advertisements, and other material.

occupations.title: Poets, Lyricists and Creative Writers
occupations.description: Create original written works, such as scripts, essays, prose, poetry or song lyrics, for publication or performance.

occupations.title: Interpreters and Translators
occupations.description: Interpret oral or sign language, or translate written text from one language into another.

occupations.title: Court Reporters and Simultaneous Captioners
occupations.description: Use verbatim methods and equipment to capture, store, retrieve, and transcribe pretrial and trial proceedings or other information. Includes stenocaptioners who operate computerized stenographic captioning equipment to provide captions of live or prerecorded broadcasts for hearing-impaired viewers.

occupations.title: Media and Communication Workers, All Other
occupations.description: All media and communication workers not listed separately.

occupations.title: Audio and Video Technicians
occupations.description: Set up, maintain, and dismantle audio and video equipment, such as microphones, sound speakers, connecting wires and cables, sound and mixing boards, video cameras, video monitors and servers, and related electronic equipment for live or recorded events, such as concerts, meetings, conventions, presentations, podcasts, news conferences, and sporting events.

titles.text: AV Production Specialist (Audio Visual Production Specialist)
Event AV Operator (Event Audio Visual Operator)

occupations.title: Broadcast Technicians
occupations.description: Set up, operate, and maintain the electronic equipment used to acquire, edit, and transmit audio and video for radio or television programs. Control and adjust incoming and outgoing broadcast signals to regulate sound volume, signal strength, and signal clarity. Operate satellite, microwave, or other transmitter equipment to broadcast radio or television programs.

titles.text: Radio Frequency Test Technician (Radio Frequency Test Tech)

occupations.title: Sound Engineering Technicians
occupations.description: Assemble and operate equipment to record, synchronize, mix, edit, or reproduce sound, including music, voices, or sound effects, for theater, video, film, television, podcasts, sporting events, and other productions.

titles.text: Audio DSP Engineer (Audio Digital Signal Processor Engineer)
Public Address System Installer (PA System Installer)
Public Address System Mechanic (PA System Mechanic)

occupations.title: Lighting Technicians
occupations.description: Set up, maintain, and dismantle light fixtures, lighting control devices, and the associated lighting electrical and rigging equipment used for photography, television, film, video, and live productions. May focus or operate light fixtures, or attach color filters or other lighting accessories.

titles.text: Sound and Lighting Technician (Sound and Lighting Tech)

occupations.title: Photographers
occupations.description: Photograph people, landscapes, merchandise, or other subjects. May use lighting equipment to enhance a subject's appearance. May use editing software to produce finished images and prints. Includes commercial and industrial photographers, scientific photographers, and photojournalists.

occupations.title: Camera Operators, Television, Video, and Film
occupations.description: Operate television, video, or film camera to record images or scenes for television, video, or film productions.

titles.text: Electronic News Gathering Camera Operator (ENG Camera Operator)
Remotely Piloted Aircraft Camera Operator (RPA Camera Operator)

occupations.title: Film and Video Editors
occupations.description: Edit moving images on film, video, or other media. May work with a producer or director to organize images for final production. May edit or synchronize soundtracks with images.

occupations.title: Media and Communication Equipment Workers, All Other
occupations.description: All media and communication equipment workers not listed separately.

occupations.title: Chiropractors
occupations.description: Assess, treat, and care for patients by manipulation of spine and musculoskeletal system. May provide spinal adjustment or address sacral or pelvic misalignment.

occupations.title: Dentists, General
occupations.description: Examine, diagnose, and treat diseases, injuries, and malformations of teeth and gums. May treat diseases of nerve, pulp, and other dental tissues affecting oral hygiene and retention of teeth. May fit dental appliances or provide preventive care.

occupations.title: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons
occupations.description: Perform surgery and related procedures on the hard and soft tissues of the oral and maxillofacial regions to treat diseases, injuries, or defects. May diagnose problems of the oral and maxillofacial regions. May perform surgery to improve function or appearance.

occupations.title: Orthodontists
occupations.description: Examine, diagnose, and treat dental malocclusions and oral cavity anomalies. Design and fabricate appliances to realign teeth and jaws to produce and maintain normal function and to improve appearance.

occupations.title: Prosthodontists
occupations.description: Diagnose, treat, rehabilitate, design, and fit prostheses that maintain oral function, health, and appearance for patients with clinical conditions associated with teeth, oral and maxillofacial tissues, or the jaw.

occupations.title: Dentists, All Other Specialists
occupations.description: All dentists not listed separately.

occupations.title: Dietitians and Nutritionists
occupations.description: Plan and conduct food service or nutritional programs to assist in the promotion of health and control of disease. May supervise activities of a department providing quantity food services, counsel individuals, or conduct nutritional research.

occupations.title: Optometrists
occupations.description: Diagnose, manage, and treat conditions and diseases of the human eye and visual system. Examine eyes and visual system, diagnose problems or impairments, prescribe corrective lenses, and provide treatment. May prescribe therapeutic drugs to treat specific eye conditions.

occupations.title: Pharmacists
occupations.description: Dispense drugs prescribed by physicians and other health practitioners and provide information to patients about medications and their use. May advise physicians and other health practitioners on the selection, dosage, interactions, and side effects of medications.

occupations.title: Physician Assistants
occupations.description: Provide healthcare services typically performed by a physician, under the supervision of a physician. Conduct complete physicals, provide treatment, and counsel patients. May, in some cases, prescribe medication. Must graduate from an accredited educational program for physician assistants.

titles.text: Emergency Medicine Physician Assistant (Emergency Medicine PA)
Family Medicine PA (Family Medicine Physician Assistant)
Surgical Critical Care Physician Assistant (Surgical Critical Care PA)
Urgent Care PA (Urgent Care Physician Assistant)

occupations.title: Anesthesiologist Assistants
occupations.description: Assist anesthesiologists in the administration of anesthesia for surgical and non-surgical procedures. Monitor patient status and provide patient care during surgical treatment.

occupations.title: Podiatrists
occupations.description: Diagnose and treat diseases and deformities of the human foot.

titles.text: Doctor of Podiatric Medicine and Surgery (DPM and Surgery)

occupations.title: Occupational Therapists
occupations.description: Assess, plan, and organize rehabilitative programs that help build or restore vocational, homemaking, and daily living skills, as well as general independence, to persons with disabilities or developmental delays. Use therapeutic techniques, adapt the individual's environment, teach skills, and modify specific tasks that present barriers to the individual.

titles.text: Acute Care OT (Acute Care Occupational Therapist)
Home Care Occupational Therapist (Home Care OT)
Pediatrics and Acute Care Occupational Therapist

occupations.title: Low Vision Therapists, Orientation and Mobility Specialists, and Vision Rehabilitation Therapists
occupations.description: Provide therapy to patients with visual impairments to improve their functioning in daily life activities. May train patients in activities such as computer use, communication skills, or home management skills.

titles.text: Blind Orientation and Mobility Therapist (Blind O and M Therapist)
Orientation and Mobility Instructor (O and M Instructor)
Orientation and Mobility Specialist (O and M Specialist)

occupations.title: Physical Therapists
occupations.description: Assess, plan, organize, and participate in rehabilitative programs that improve mobility, relieve pain, increase strength, and improve or correct disabling conditions resulting from disease or injury.

titles.text: Acute Care PT (Acute Care Physical Therapist)
Home Care Physical Therapist (Home Care PT)
Home Health Physical Therapist (Home Health PT)
Outpatient Orthopedics Physical Therapist (Outpatient Ortho PT)
Outpatient Travel Physical Therapist (Outpatient Travel PT)
Skilled Nursing Facility Physical Therapist (SNF PT)

occupations.title: Radiation Therapists
occupations.description: Provide radiation therapy to patients as prescribed by a radiation oncologist according to established practices and standards. Duties may include reviewing prescription and diagnosis; acting as liaison with physician and supportive care personnel; preparing equipment, such as immobilization, treatment, and protection devices; and maintaining records, reports, and files. May assist in dosimetry procedures and tumor localization.

titles.text: Computed Tomography Simulation Therapist (CT Simulation Therapist)
Radiation Oncology Registered Nurse (Radiation Oncology RN)

occupations.title: Recreational Therapists
occupations.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate medically-approved recreation programs for patients in hospitals, nursing homes, or other institutions. Activities include sports, trips, dramatics, social activities, and crafts. May assess a patient condition and recommend appropriate recreational activity.

occupations.title: Respiratory Therapists
occupations.description: Assess, treat, and care for patients with breathing disorders. Assume primary responsibility for all respiratory care modalities, including the supervision of respiratory therapy technicians. Initiate and conduct therapeutic procedures; maintain patient records; and select, assemble, check, and operate equipment.

titles.text: NICU RT (Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Respiratory Therapist)

occupations.title: Speech-Language Pathologists
occupations.description: Assess and treat persons with speech, language, voice, and fluency disorders. May select alternative communication systems and teach their use. May perform research related to speech and language problems.

titles.text: Home Health SLP (Home Health Speech Language Pathologist)
SLP CF (Speech Language Pathologist Clinical Fellow)
SNF RN (Skilled Nursing Facility Registered Nurse)
Virtual School SLP (Virtual School Speech Language Pathologist)

occupations.title: Exercise Physiologists
occupations.description: Assess, plan, or implement fitness programs that include exercise or physical activities such as those designed to improve cardiorespiratory function, body composition, muscular strength, muscular endurance, or flexibility.

occupations.title: Therapists, All Other
occupations.description: All therapists not listed separately.

occupations.title: Art Therapists
occupations.description: Plan or conduct art therapy sessions or programs to improve clients' physical, cognitive, or emotional well-being.

occupations.title: Music Therapists
occupations.description: Plan, organize, direct, or assess clinical and evidenced-based music therapy interventions to positively influence individuals' physical, psychological, cognitive, or behavioral status.

occupations.title: Veterinarians
occupations.description: Diagnose, treat, or research diseases and injuries of animals. Includes veterinarians who conduct research and development, inspect livestock, or care for pets and companion animals.

titles.text: Laboratory Animal Care Veterinarian (Lab Animal Care Vet)
Veterinary Virus Serum Inspector (Vet Virus Serum Inspector)

occupations.title: Registered Nurses
occupations.description: Assess patient health problems and needs, develop and implement nursing care plans, and maintain medical records. Administer nursing care to ill, injured, convalescent, or disabled patients. May advise patients on health maintenance and disease prevention or provide case management. Licensing or registration required.

titles.text: Emergency Department RN (Emergency Department Registered Nurse)
Home Health RN (Home Health Registered Nurse)
L and D RN (Labor and Delivery Registered Nurse)
Med- Surg Travel RN (Medical Surgical Travel Registered Nurse)
Med-Surg Telemetry RN (Medical Surgical Telemetry Registered Nurse)
Neonatal Intensive Care Registered Nurse (NICU RN)
PACU RN (Post Anesthesia Care Unit Registered Nurse)
PACU RN (Post-Anesthesia Care Unit Registered Nurse)
RN Case Manager (Registered Nurse Case Manager)
Telemetry Travel RN (Telemetry Travel Registered Nurse)

occupations.title: Acute Care Nurses
occupations.description: Provide advanced nursing care for patients with acute conditions such as heart attacks, respiratory distress syndrome, or shock. May care for pre- and post-operative patients or perform advanced, invasive diagnostic or therapeutic procedures.

titles.text: Cardiovascular ICU Nurse (Cardiovascular Intense Care Unit Nurse)
Cardiovascular Surgery Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (Cardiovascular Surgery ACNP)
ICU RN (Intensive Care Unit Registered Nurse)
ICU Travel RN (Intensive Care Unit Travel Registered Nurse)
PACU RN (Post Anesthesia Care Unit Registered Nurse)
PACU Travel RN (Post Anesthesia Care Unit Travel Registered Nurse)
PCU RN (Progressive Care Unit Registered Nurse)
Progressive Care RN (Progressive Care Registered Nurse)
Screening Unit RN (Screening Unit Registered Nurse)
Step Down RN (Step Down Registered Nurse)
Vascular Access Registered Nurse (Vascular Access RN)

occupations.title: Advanced Practice Psychiatric Nurses
occupations.description: Assess, diagnose, and treat individuals and families with mental health or substance use disorders or the potential for such disorders. Apply therapeutic activities, including the prescription of medication, per state regulations, and the administration of psychotherapy.

titles.text: Adult PMHNP (Adult Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner)
Adult Psychiatric Mental Health APRN (Adult Psychiatric Mental Health Advanced Practice Registered Nurse)
Board Certified Psychiatric Mental Health Clinical Nurse Specialist (BC PMH-CNS)
Family Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (Family Psychiatric Mental Health NP)
PMH-APRN (Psychiatric Mental Health Advanced Practice Registered Nurse)
Psychiatry APRN (Psychiatry Advanced Practice Registered Nurse)
Travel Psychiatric RN (Travel Psychiatric Registered Nurse)

occupations.title: Critical Care Nurses
occupations.description: Provide specialized nursing care for patients in critical or coronary care units.

titles.text: CCU RN (Cardiac Care Unit Registered Nurse)
CCU RN (Coronary Care Unit Registered Nurse)
CCU RN (Critical Care Unit Registered Nurse)
CVICU RN (Cardiovascular Intensive Care Unit Registered Nurse)
ICU Critical Care NP (Intensive Care Unit Critical Care Nurse Practitioner)
ICU Travel RN (Intensive Care Unit Travel Registered Nurse)

Intensive Care Unit Registered Nurse (ICU RN)
